channel.title: World News
channel.description: Aggregated headlines linking to original publishers

item.title: Rivers in the sky are raining down on the Pacific Northwest. What are they?
item.description: Atmospheric rivers are large bands of water vapor in the sky. They are dumping trillions of gallons of water on Washington and Oregon, just as high tides and winds batter shorelines. (Image credit: David Ryder)

item.title: Potential 'national security crisis' as Nvidia ex-CEO summoned by US Congress
item.description: What began as an investigation into the now former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is turning into what could be shaping up to be a "national security crisis", says France 24's correspondent in Los Angeles Wassim Cornet, after US lawmakers called on Huang to face their questions in December. Huang resigned as head of the chip giant over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy. The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia's market valuation.

item.title: SpaceX's giant rocket may leave NASA in the dust
item.description: As it races to develop its new massive rocket, the space launch company is preparing to retire NASA's main ride to the International Space Station. (Image credit: Eric Gay)

item.title: Why even a fraction of a degree can escalate climate change impacts
item.description: Countries are not meeting their goal of limiting climate change to 1.5 degrees Celsius. How much hotter the planet gets makes a profound difference for the impacts the world could see. (Image credit: Sirachai Arunrugstichai)

item.title: These two voter turnout trends explain what happened across the South in the election
item.description: In six states across the Deep South, a drastic swing to the left this election was driven by high Black voter turnout and compounded by a sharp decline in voting rates across Republican-heavy areas. (Image credit: Brandon Bell/Getty Images)

item.title: These swing voters have low expectations for divided government
item.description: Key voters in North Carolina are pessimistic the blue wave flipping control of Congress will solve their economic woes. Many say President Trump will be the chief obstacle. (Image credit: A.M. Stewart)

item.title: Fill in the blank in the quiz: NASA will pay astronauts $___ to live on the moon
item.description: Plus: Have you been following news about cars and Pete Hegseth this week?

item.title: The cost of college is confusing. Some schools are trying to change that
item.description: Many Americans have soured on higher education because of how frustratingly hard it is to figure out what they will pay to attend. (Image credit: Oliver Parini for The Hechinger Report)

item.title: Why is Google cutting off Search from AI-free schools? Here are some theories
item.description: The forthcoming move has left some parents and educators frustrated and wondering about the company's motivations. (Image credit: Don Ryan/AP)

item.title: 'One of the biggest outages ever': Disruption to Microsoft services enters second day
item.description: An outage of Microsoft services such as Outlook, Teams and Copilot that began on Thursday continued to cause disruption to users around the world on Friday as the tech giant struggled to fix server problems it blamed for the problems. France 24’s tech correspondent Peter O’Brien takes a look at what we know about the outage which, given its scale and duration, makes it one of the “biggest ever”, he says.

item.title: Rosalía and Milo J take top awards as Daddy Yankee is paid tribute at Latin Grammys
item.description: The night was filled with music and surprises. Rosalía opened the show with medley of tracks and elaborate dancing, and Milo J appeared with a colorful Uruguayan theatrical ensemble. (Image credit: Kevin Winter)

item.title: Microsoft Outlook outage updates: Latest on email as services go down
item.description: Microsoft is reporting "issues" with users accessing Outlook and Teams.

item.title: Winter is coming: Putin seeks to 'hammer Ukrainians, their power grid, their water supplies'
item.description: As renewed diplomatic efforts seek to bring an end to Russia's war on Ukraine, the prospect of a negotiated settlement remains unlikely due to Russia's irreconcilable territorial demands, competing visions of European security and an increasingly unpredictable and pro-Moscow US. For Mark Galeotti, Executive Director of Mayak Intelligence and Honorary Professor at University College London's School of Slavonic and East European Studies, Moscow's maximalist vision conceals a more complex negotiating strategy. And the territorial dispute over Donbas presents a particularly formidable obstacle. Putin's determination to claim control over the entirety of the region confronts Ukraine's refusal to surrender territory it continues to hold.

item.title: Who will inherit 007's licence to thrill? 'The world is not enough' in the hunt for James Bond
item.description: More than six decades after James Bond first appeared on the big screen, the search for Daniel Craig's successor has become a revealing debate about the future of one of cinema's most enduring, and endearing, franchises. "From the cold-blooded sexual magnetism of Sean Connery to the more tongue-in-cheek take of Roger Moore, to Daniel Craig's gritty realism, there's really a James Bond for everyone." But who will inherit the licence to thrill? FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell takes us on this exciting edge-of-your-seat adventure with a "view to a kill". Should Bond remain faithful to his traditional identity, or reinvent himself to reflect changing attitudes towards gender, diversity and contemporary heroism?

item.title: 2027 AFCON Qualifiers: Top guns Senegal, Cameroon, Ivory Coast deliver
item.description: Africa's heavyweights are delivering in the 2027 AFCON qualifiers. Senegal marked Patrick Vieira's first home game with an emphatic win over Sudan, while Cameroon and Ivory Coast took further steps towards qualification.

item.title: Manchester United 'agree two-and-a-half-year deal with Mauricio Pochettino'
item.description: Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino have agreed a deal for him to take over as head coach with the team in the Premier League's relegation zone.

item.title: What we know about victims of deadly Brooklyn building collapse
item.description: Two children, ages 9 and 10, were among those killed, according to authorities.

item.title: Live: Microsoft 'not aware of any malicious activity' behind global Outlook outage
item.description: Microsoft's Outlook email service has been disrupted since late Thursday as the tech giant struggles to fix issues with its servers, hitting businesses and government agencies that use the popular work platforms in 74 countries and territories. The company said Friday it had not found any malicious activity causing the outage and blamed elevated infrastructure loads. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV meets abuse victims in Peru, says Church must make 'amends'
item.description: Pope Leo XIV met six victims of clerical abuse in Peru on Thursday, including people linked to disbanded group Sodalitium Christianae Vitae. The US-born pontiff also urged the Catholic Church to make amends to survivors and strengthen protections against abuse as he returned to the country where he served as a missionary and bishop for nearly two decades.

item.title: Haitian police retake national stadium after two years of gang control
item.description: Haitian security forces regained control of the country's main football stadium Thursday after two years under gang control, with Salvadoran troops taking over security at the venue. El Salvador deployed 2,000 soldiers to Haiti following an ambush that left four of its troops missing.

item.title: Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton has finalized his divorce
item.description: An attorney for Republican Ken Paxton says Texas' outgoing attorney general has finalized his divorce

item.title: Live: Zelensky and Kushner confirm that Europe will join next round of Russia-Ukraine talks
item.description: US envoy and President ​Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner said on Thursday Russia and ​Ukraine ‌agreed ⁠to expand the next ‌round of talks to include ⁠European nations, who will debate whether their envoy should be one individual or more and who should represent them at a summit in Dublin on Friday. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.

item.title: WATCH: SS United States sinks off of Florida coast to become artificial reef
item.description: The ocean liner, larger than the Titanic, was sunk into the ocean to create the world's largest artificial reef.

item.title: WATCH: Punch the Monkey caring for new baby monkey at Ichikawa City Zoo
item.description: Punch, the monkey who captivated the world after he was abandoned by his mother and shunned by other monkeys at a zoo in Japan, was seen taking interest in a new baby macaque in his enclosure.

item.title: FBI seizes $1.2bn stolen in Binance cryptocurrency hack
item.description: The FBI has seized more than $1.2bn (£910m) of cryptocurrency stolen from Binance last month.

item.title: ‘Peruvian pope’ Leo XIV comes home to a country that shaped his life and faith through 'hardship'
item.description: François Picard is pleased to welcome Victor Casallo, Director of the Department of Philosophical and Theological Studies at Antonio Ruiz de Montoya University. Can a Pope shaped by Peru's history of political violence, social inequality and religious activism help a deeply polarized nation heal and rediscover the possibility of dialogue? "We tend to see the other person not as someone who holds a different opinion, but as an enemy." Casallo argues that Pope Leo, the first American-born pontiff's identity cannot be understood through his Chicago origins alone.

item.title: US soldier accused of spying for Russia identified: Source
item.description: US officer who was arrested in the UK on suspicion of spying for Russia is 41-year-old Lt. Col. Brandon Tyner, according to a source familiar with the investigation.

item.title: New York building collapse kills eight, including two children
item.description: Eight people, including two children, were killed when a residential building collapsed into an adjacent construction site in Brooklyn on Wednesday. Firefighters spent hours searching the rubble overnight before declaring the operation over on Thursday as authorities launched an investigation into the disaster.

item.title: Russia using 'illegal and unethical means, knows Europe won't use same means back', expert says
item.description: There are mounting concerns across Europe that recent hoax threats and cyber attacks could be part of a massive hybrid warfare campaign. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Elisabeth Braw, Senior Fellow with the Atlantic Council’s Transatlantic Security Initiative. She says that Russia's aim is to "increase its power at the expense of European countries and the easiest way to do that is to constantly wage this dirty war against European countries, using illegal and unethical means, because Russia knows that we are not going to use the same means back".

item.title: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after mounting scandals
item.description: Jensen Huang, long considered the face of the AI revolution, has resigned as Nvidia's President, CEO and board member as sandals over his romantic affairs wiped hundreds of billions of dollars from the company's market value in a matter of days. US lawmakers signal they'll likely push for tighter export restrictions for AI chips. Meanwhile, the rapid buildout of AI data centre is sparking anger and worries among French communities.

item.title: Mauritania fishing boats falsely portrayed as migrant fleet bound for Spain
item.description: Spain’s Canary Islands are facing renewed pressure from migrant arrivals, with local authorities declaring a state of emergency. Against this backdrop, a viral video claims to show thousands of boats in Mauritania amassing at the port, that users said was "ready to set sail" to carry migrants to the archipelago. But the satellite images are misleading: they show a traditional fishing port, not a fleet of migrant vessels. Vedika Bahl explains in Truth or Fake.

item.title: Colom’s historic Senate win could reshape Mississippi’s political future: Analysis
item.description: The question is whether his victory can establish a lasting realignment.

item.title: Across Africa: Tunisians drawn into Russia's war with Ukraine
item.description: This week: A new report says more than 1,400 Africans have been recruited to fight for Russia in Ukraine since 2023. Also, as South Africa races to become Africa's digital gateway, a growing backlash is emerging in Cape Town. And music, dance and theatre lit up Abéché as the city's arts festival in Chad drew crowds of young spectators.

item.title: Ngo criticizes UN's response to massacre in South Sudan
item.description: In tonight's edition, Amnesty International accuses both the government and UN peacekeepers of failing to protect civilians during a massacre in South Sudan that killed over 200 people. Also, more than a thousand people are prosecuted for illegal mining in Guinea. And a century after French colonial troops killed him, a Malagasy king has finally come home.

item.title: 'There's no such thing as safe' in contact sports, brain injury expert says
item.description: Discussing the issue of contact sports and the threat to sports men and women of all ages, particularly in the light of the recent death, just last month, of a 17-year-old French woman after a head collision on the rugby field, FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Dr Daniel H Daneshvar, Associate Professor at Harvard Medical School. He says that "there's not such thing as safe" in contact sports, explaining that "if you get a lot of repeated hits to the head, then you're at risk for problems later in life, both in the near term and the long term".

item.title: Republicans push for Jensen Huang's testimony following Nvidia CEO's resignation
item.description: "I don't think he's got anything to hide now. Let it fly," Rep. Burchett said.

item.title: Israeli strike on Gaza hospital kills six, including surgeon, medics say
item.description: Israeli fire killed 11 people in Gaza on Thursday, six of them in the bombing of Nasser hospital in south Gaza early in the day, health officials said, the deadliest single strike since Israel's elections last month. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Dr Goher Rahbour, a surgeon working at the Nasser Hospital.

item.title: Zelensky warns Europe over US-Russia talks on broader security arrangements
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky warned European leaders Thursday to be wary of discussions between the United States and Russia about a new security arrangement for the continent. Before launching the war in 2022, the Kremlin delivered an ultimatum to NATO on Europe's security arrangements which included demands for the alliance to withdraw forces from eastern Europe and stop accepting new members. FRANCE 24's Caroline Baum reports.

item.title: Plugged-in planet? COP31 host Turkey leads charge for electrification
item.description: It’s sweater weather in Paris. But even though November brings brisk temperatures and fall foliage, it doesn’t mean last summer’s record heat should fade from our memories. One of the suggested reasons why students are so boiling mad is the hell they endured back in June in overheated classrooms and baking shoebox apartments.

item.title: White House reportedly discussing Howard Lutnick's future as Commerce secretary
item.description: Senior White House officials are discussing whether ​Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick should be pushed out in the wake of the spy scandal surrounding Nvidia's now ​former ‌CEO Jensen Huang, two people familiar ⁠with the situation told Reuters on Thursday. In June, Reuters reported that the Trump administration had held ⁠off from adding China’s AI startup DeepSeek, memory chipmaker CXMT and more than 100 other companies flagged as national security risks to a trade blacklist. FRANCE 24's Wassim Cornet reports from Los Angeles.
